newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: FORECAST - Singapore Dec exports up 2.9 pct - poll.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Singapore Dec exports up 2.9 pct - poll.

text.p: Singapore's non-oil exports rebounded in December thanks to a recovery in the key electronics industry, a Reuters poll of economists suggested on Thursday.
Fifteen financial institutions, surveyed between Tuesday and Thursday, produced an average forecast of a rise of 2.9 percent year-on-year in nominal terms in the island's non-oil domestic exports.
This compares with a fall of 8.8 percent in November and a rise of 1.1 percent in October.
Singapore's non-oil domestic exports in November were valued at Singapore $7.28 billion (US$5.20 billion) in nominal terms.

Economists said the export recovery in December was due to the turnaround in the global electronics market, which absorbs about half Singapore's industrial production and almost 60 percent of its non-oil overseas sales.
Singapore is one of the world's biggest producers of computer chips and electronic semi-conductors.
Wholesale demand for electronics products and computer components plunged in the third quarter of 1996 with many U.S. and Asian high techology companies reducing orders.
Economists said this was mainly a cyclical downturn sparked by inventory surpluses, and they forecast demand for electronics would recover strongly worldwide by mid-1997.
But they said the first quarter of this year might still see further bad months for Asian electronics producers until the recovery gets properly under way.

Economists said U.S. electronics demand reached a low point in August or September and said they would expect a time lag of six or seven months before this cyclical trough was passed back along the supply chain to Asian primary producers.
The same Reuters poll produced an average forecast of a rise of 1.5 percent year-on-year in December in Singapore's consumer price index (CPI) of inflation.
Five of the economists polled also forecast Singapore's retail sales index (RSI) rose 0.8 percent in November.
Singapore's CPI rose 1.4 percent in November year-on-year. The RSI rose 1.1 percent in October.
Singapore's official export figures and CPI data are due to be published next week. The RSI is expected to be released on Sunday evening.
